Passing the **NCLEX-RN** or **NCLEX-PN** requires a structured study plan, consistent practice, and strategic test-taking skills. Below is a **comprehensive 8-week NCLEX to-do list** to help you prepare effectively.

---

### **📅 NCLEX To-Do List (8-Week Plan)**
*(Adjust based on your timeline—some may need 4-12 weeks.)*

#### **📌 Week 1: Assessment & Foundation**
✅ **Take a Diagnostic Test** – Identify strengths/weaknesses (UWorld, Kaplan, or Hurst).
✅ **Review NCLEX Test Plan** – Understand the exam format, question types, and content areas ([NCSBN Test Plan](https://www.ncsbn.org/nclex.htm)).
✅ **Gather Study Materials** – Choose **1-2 primary resources** (e.g., UWorld, Saunders, Kaplan, Hurst, Mark Klimek lectures).
✅ **Set a Study Schedule** – Aim for **3-5 hours/day**, 5-6 days/week.
✅ **Review Fundamentals** – Start with **basic nursing concepts** (Maslow’s, ABCs, infection control, safety, legal/ethical issues).
✅ **Begin Content Review** – Focus on **high-yield topics** (Pharm, Med-Surg, OB, Peds, Psych, Fundamentals).

#### **📌 Week 2-3: Content Mastery & Practice Questions**
✅ **Deep Dive into Weak Areas** – Use **Saunders Comprehensive Review** or **Hurst Review** for content gaps.
✅ **Do 50-75 Practice Questions Daily** – Focus on **rationale review** (UWorld is best for this).
✅ **Prioritize High-Yield Topics** (Most tested on NCLEX):
   - **Pharmacology** (Antihypertensives, Insulin, Antibiotics, Cardiac meds)
   - **Med-Surg** (Diabetes, CHF, COPD, Renal failure, Sepsis, Stroke)
   - **OB/Peds** (Preeclampsia, Newborn care, Growth & Development)
   - **Psych** (Therapeutic communication, Depression, Schizophrenia)
   - **Fundamentals** (Infection control, Delegation, Prioritization)
✅ **Watch Mark Klimek Lectures** (Free on YouTube) – Great for **prioritization & delegation**.
✅ **Take a Full-Length Practice Test** (UWorld or Kaplan) – Simulate test conditions.

#### **📌 Week 4-5: Test-Taking Strategies & Critical Thinking**
✅ **Master NCLEX Question Strategies**:
   - **Eliminate wrong answers first** (Look for "absolute" words like "always," "never").
   - **Prioritize using ABCs (Airway, Breathing, Circulation)**.
   - **Use Maslow’s Hierarchy** (Physiological needs > Safety > Love/Belonging > Esteem > Self-Actualization).
   - **Avoid "nurse knows best" answers** (NCLEX wants **client-centered care**).
✅ **Increase Practice Questions to 75-100/day** – Focus on **SATA (Select All That Apply)**.
✅ **Review Lab Values & Normal Ranges** (Electrolytes, ABGs, CBC, Coagulation).
✅ **Take Another Full-Length Practice Test** – Track progress.
✅ **Review Incorrect Answers** – Understand **why** you got them wrong.

#### **📌 Week 6: Simulated Exams & Weakness Targeting**
✅ **Take 2-3 Full-Length NCLEX Simulations** (UWorld, Kaplan, or Hurst).
✅ **Analyze Performance** – Focus on **time management** (NCLEX is **6 hours max**).
✅ **Revisit Weak Areas** – Use **flashcards (Anki, Quizlet)** for memorization.
✅ **Practice Delegation & Prioritization Questions** – Know **RN vs. LPN vs. UAP** roles.
✅ **Review NCLEX Hot Topics**:
   - **Infection Control** (Isolation precautions, PPE)
   - **Emergency Situations** (Shock, MI, Stroke, Seizures)
   - **Ethical/Legal Issues** (Informed consent, HIPAA, Advance directives)

#### **📌 Week 7: Final Review & Confidence Building**
✅ **Do 100+ Questions Daily** – Mix of **easy, medium, and hard** questions.
✅ **Review All Incorrect Answers** – Keep an **error log**.
✅ **Watch NCLEX Tips Videos** (Simple Nursing, RegisteredNurseRN on YouTube).
✅ **Memorize Key Mnemonics** (e.g., **"ROME"** for ABGs, **"MONA"** for MI).
✅ **Take a Final Full-Length Test** – Aim for **75%+** to feel confident.
✅ **Relax & Avoid Cramming** – Focus on **mental preparation**.

#### **📌 Week 8: Test Day Preparation**
✅ **Register for NCLEX** – Ensure **ATI or Pearson VUE** has your authorization.
✅ **Gather Test Day Essentials**:
   - **ATI/Pearson VUE Authorization Email**
   - **Government-Issued ID** (Passport, Driver’s License)
   - **Comfortable Clothes** (Layers for temperature control)
   - **Snacks & Water** (For breaks)
✅ **Plan Your Route** – Know the **test center location** and **traffic conditions**.
✅ **Get Good Sleep** – **No all-nighters!** (Aim for **7-8 hours** before the exam).
✅ **Review Last-Minute Tips**:
   - **Flag tough questions** and come back later.
   - **Don’t overthink** – First instinct is usually right.
   - **Stay calm** – The exam **adapts to your ability**.
✅ **Take the NCLEX!** – **You’ve got this!** 🎉

---

### **🔥 Bonus Tips for NCLEX Success**
✔ **Use UWorld** – Best for **rationales & SATA questions**.
✔ **Mark Klimek Lectures** – Free & **gold standard** for prioritization.
✔ **Saunders Comprehensive Review** – Best for **content review**.
✔ **Practice SATA Questions Daily** – NCLEX loves these!
✔ **Stay Positive** – Confidence is key!
✔ **Trust the Process** – The exam **stops when it’s 95% sure** of your competence.

---

### **📚 Recommended Resources**
| **Resource** | **Best For** |
|-------------|------------|
| **UWorld** | Practice questions & rationales |
| **Saunders Comprehensive Review** | Content review |
| **Mark Klimek Lectures (YouTube)** | Prioritization & delegation |
| **Hurst Review** | Content + test strategies |
| **Kaplan NCLEX Prep** | Full-length practice tests |
| **Simple Nursing (YouTube)** | Quick review videos |
| **Anki/Quizlet** | Flashcards for memorization |

---

### **💡 Final Encouragement**
- **The NCLEX is not about memorization—it’s about critical thinking.**
- **You’ve already passed nursing school—this is just the final step!**
- **Stay consistent, trust your prep, and you WILL pass!** 🚀

Would you like a **customized study plan** based on your weak areas? Let me know! 😊
